abstract: Perturbational spatial atlases have begun to map regenerative dynamics in a variety of tissues, yet lung remodeling has not been characterized at comparable spatial and temporal resolution. Post-pneumonectomy lung regeneration (PPLR) provides a tractable mammalian model for tissue regeneration that can be studied in situ. Here, we present a spatiotemporal perturbational atlas of PPLR in Rattus norvegicus, combining single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNAseq), high-resolution spatial transcriptomics (10x Genomics Xenium), and NICHES-based spatial tissue connectomics. We observe three distinct tissue architectures at successive timepoints after pneumonectomy, each characterized by coordinated shifts in local cellular composition and intercellular signaling. At Day 3 (D3), a line of interstitial macrophages colocalizes directly beneath an intact mesothelium among active mechanotransductive and inflammatory signaling. We also observe the unexpected appearance of a transitional remodeling cellular community at D7 which appears largely absent at later timepoints, marked by fibrosis- mimetic signaling. At D14, an alveologenic architecture at distal lung tissue displays a connectivity signature consistent with active de novo growth, distinct from baseline homeostasis. Our findings establish a spatiotemporal map of multicellular architecture during regenerative lung remodeling and introduce a generalizable framework for spatial connectomic analysis to be used in perturbational tissue systems biology.
